hyperedges.label: UI thread plus receiver, runner, and submitter share one PassingCommand channel

nodes.label: Content-Hash Compile Cache
nodes.rationale: Compile once and cache the binary by source hash plus flags so unchanged code replays every case instantly, with 1ms polling, per-case timing, and hard TLE kills.

nodes.label: In-Memory Smoke Case
nodes.rationale: Run on a file with no stored cases adds one empty input/expected case so compile and crash can still be checked. Only one run is active; Esc, edit, delete, or a new problem cancels it and kills the child process group.

nodes.label: syspolicyd Latency Fix
nodes.rationale: macOS syspolicyd adds about 200ms when running newly compiled binaries. Adding Zed and the terminal under Developer Tools and Full Disk Access drops execution latency to about 3-4ms.

nodes.label: ZCH TUI Screenshot Showing WA Verdict (1ms)
nodes.norm_label: zch tui screenshot showing wa verdict (1ms)

nodes.label: CAPTCHA Handling
nodes.rationale: When Codeforces serves an invisible CAPTCHA, the TUI alerts the user and Safari foregrounds itself; after the user solves it, live verdict polling resumes automatically.

nodes.label: One-Key Codeforces Submission
nodes.rationale: A confirmation modal shows every detail, then async verdicts stream into the Submissions bar. Safari tabs are tracked by URL with INTERRUPTED, TIMED OUT, and a hard 5-minute timeout.

nodes.label: Validated Compile-Flag Tags
nodes.rationale: Flags must start with -, duplicates and unknown -std= versions are rejected, and lists are stored per language in ~/.zch/config.json. No -std, -O2, or warning flags are added implicitly. Codeforces ids: C++17 → 54, C++20 → 89, C++23 → 91. Deleting either half of a -include-pch pair removes both.

nodes.label: Multi-Language Support
nodes.rationale: C++, Python 3, and Java. No hidden flags: -O2, -std=c++20, and -include-pch are entered as individually validated tags so the Codeforces language id follows the user's -std= tag.

nodes.label: Output Truncation and Spill
nodes.rationale: Outside edit mode, raw output is cut to a ~24 KB preview and panes show at most 300 lines / 24k characters; huge WA skips the character diff. The large pane dialog keeps full output up to 10 MB / 20,000 lines, then spills to a temp file and diffs the visible page.

nodes.label: Precompiled Headers
nodes.rationale: Compiling bits/stdc++.h dominates a cold run. A shared PCH cuts it from roughly 0.3s to 0.1s on an M-series Mac, but zch adds no flags itself; the user must pass -include-pch. Standard, architecture, and compiler version must match, and Homebrew GCC cannot use a Clang-built PCH.

nodes.label: Problem Auto-Parse
nodes.rationale: Payloads on 127.0.0.1:10043 create a file from ~/.zch/boilerplate.cpp with a // URL: header, store tests in ~/.zch/.tc/, and open the file in Zed. Same sanitized filenames get a short URL suffix so tests and binaries do not overwrite.

nodes.label: std-with-pbds
nodes.rationale: Apple Clang does not ship bits/stdc++.h or policy-based data structures. The std-with-pbds helper repo sets both up for Apple Clang and supplies the header used to build the PCH.

nodes.label: Live TUI Dashboard
nodes.rationale: Directory bar, message console, verdict cards, and a footer that always shows the current mode plus its keys so status never resizes the rest of the UI.

nodes.label: Instant Verdict Chips
nodes.rationale: Each case gets AC/WA/TLE/RE/CE chips and auto-collapses on AC; WA marks differing characters in red so the mismatch is visible without leaving the TUI.

nodes.label: ZCH
nodes.rationale: Single Rust binary TUI that receives competitive-programming problems, times samples, and submits to Codeforces from one local dashboard.

nodes.label: zch send Command API
nodes.rationale: Zed tasks drive the running TUI over HTTP (send r, send s) with the active ZED_FILE and report real success or refusal reasons. ZCH_PORT overrides the default port 10043.

nodes.label: Zed Keymap Macros
nodes.rationale: cmd-r spawns the dashboard in the center pane then splits right with Zed's built-in Split Right so the TUI sits beside the code without changing dock settings.

nodes.label: Single-Channel Actor Model
nodes.rationale: The UI thread owns all state. Receiver, runner, and submitter workers only exchange PassingCommand envelopes on one channel and never hold a handle to another worker.

nodes.label: Why Safari Only
nodes.rationale: Submission automation must run JavaScript in the background without stealing focus. Only Safari supports this natively via AppleScript; other browsers would foreground the window mid-solve.
